---
title: "Hands-on: Breaking Networks on Purpose"
---

The theory says scale-free networks shrug off random failure and collapse under targeted attack. Here you make that happen and measure it.

## What you will build

1. Measure connectivity as the fraction of nodes left in the largest component.
2. Simulate random failure, averaging over many runs to get confidence intervals.
3. Simulate targeted attack, both with a fixed ranking and with degrees recomputed after every removal.
4. Plot robustness profiles and reduce each to a single R-index.
5. Compare network types — random, scale-free, lattice — under both attack modes.

## What to watch for

- Run random failure once and it looks smooth; run it fifty times and the variance is the story. Always plot the spread, not just the mean.
- Compare adaptive against fixed-order attack on the same network. The gap is the value of information to an attacker.
- Check your measured threshold against f_c = 1 - 1/(kappa - 1) from the appendix.
